A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MolLangBench and retain matching task formulations, datasets, and evaluations. The main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on molecular recognition, editing, and generation, alongside category-level results and manual-versus-OCR evaluation.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds GPT-5 and chemistry-specific model evaluations, extended-set results, prompt sensitivity tests, and repeated-run measurements.

M1.justification: The task interfaces and original annotation pipeline remain unchanged. Appendix A.6 introduces an alternative curation procedure for extended sets, using one annotator and one validator with self-checking and feedback, instead of the core pipeline's two annotators and two validators.

E1.justification: Appendix A.8 adds editing test scenarios using alternative SMILES enumerations and paraphrased general and chemical instructions. The underlying UniChem source, chemical domain, and task families remain unchanged; the extended sets primarily increase sample counts within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds GPT-5 across all three task families and evaluates ChemDFM-13B, ChemLLM-20B-Chat-SFT, and Galactica-120B on editing (Table S4). Earlier comparators remain evaluated; GPT-4.1 disappears from the selected main tables but remains in the complete appendix comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds separate evaluation of 200 extended editing instances and 200 extended generation instances with o3 and GPT-5. New controlled experiments use five SMILES variants per editing instance, 200 general-language paraphrases, and 100 chemical-terminology rewrites. Core pass@1, validity, and localization metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.8 adds quantitative tests of sensitivity to molecular serialization, general wording, and chemical terminology, examining whether these variations explain editing failures. Earlier category-level editing results, tokenization examples, OCR analysis, and image-generation error cases are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 reports dispersion of rankings across tasks but no repeated-run accuracy uncertainty. v2 newly reports mean and standard deviation over five o3 executions of every task (Table S5), plus variability across five SMILES variants. GPT-5 is explicitly excluded from repeated-run analysis because of cost.

E6.justification: v2 adds GPT-5 recognition/localization averages of 0.923/0.862, editing accuracy of 0.855, and generation accuracy of 0.430, plus extended-set, chemistry-model, and robustness results. Most earlier scores persist. However, Table S6 interchanges DeepSeek-R1 and R1-70B quaternary-carbon scores, 0.780/0.680 and 0.440/0.330, relative to v1 Table S3, creating a conflict with v2 Table 1.

T1.justification: Section 2 retains the same mathematical mappings for recognition, editing, and generation. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the added appendix material introduces no substantive mathematical definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction update the headline empirical claim from o3 to GPT-5 as the strongest evaluated model, with higher reported accuracy levels. The central contribution remains the same precise three-task benchmark, and the conclusion that leading models struggle with molecular structure tasks is retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that prompt wording has limited influence, additional molecule-language data may be needed, and chemistry-specific models fail through poor instruction following (A.7–A.8). It also explains reduced peer review through annotator experience and acknowledges weaker extended-set validation. Existing tokenization and molecular-assembly explanations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies a code-access link, model snapshot dates, an R1-70B commit identifier, and Azure/vLLM execution information (A.4, Table S3). It documents the extended annotation workflow and corrects the core editing annotation estimate from 40 to 30 minutes. These disclosures substantially improve reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds references covering GPT-5, SMILES enumeration, ChemDFM, ChemLLM, Galactica, and recent scientific reasoning benchmarks. Its principal positioning against ambiguous molecule-description datasets and conventional chemical prediction approaches remains essentially unchanged in Section 5.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the six-section narrative are retained. Changes include localized wording edits, author-list updates, author-year citations, expanded and reordered appendix sections, and renaming the editing category 'Isomerization' to 'Tautomerization.' The revision does not extensively rewrite the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds the simplified-pipeline diagram and tables for model snapshots, chemistry-specific comparisons, and repeated-run statistics. Result tables accommodate GPT-5 and extended-set entries; the ranking plot moves from Figure 6 to Figure S4 and incorporates GPT-5. Document-wide typography and headers change, and retained examples are rearranged.

improvement.justification: Model snapshots and code-access information, controlled prompt tests, and five-run uncertainty estimates improve reproducibility and empirical support beyond v1. The gain is moderated by less independent validation for extended data and new reporting errors: swapped quaternary-carbon entries in Table S6 and a stereochemistry claim overlooking GPT-4.1's retained 0.670 score. The original carefully validated core remains intact.
